abstract.t: This document is a subordinate specification of the PIC Specification 0.2. It defines COSS Temporal Evidence: a protocol-neutral way to bind evidence from several security coordinates to one causal execution occurrence. A record may reference PIC authority-continuity evidence, information-flow evidence, runtime provenance, geographic evidence, or other profile-defined evidence without absorbing the semantics of those systems.

The central rule is simple: one occurrence, one causal history, several independently verified coordinates. An authenticated digest reference proves that a record committed to exact artifact bytes; it does not prove that the referenced claim is true. Each required artifact remains subject to its own verifier, while the COSS record prevents valid evidence from unrelated executions from being mixed and presented as evidence of one effect.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: An effect can be authorized in one dimension and forbidden in another. A mail service may receive both a valid permission to send and bytes derived from confidential data. The permission answers what authority may continue. It does not answer where the bytes may flow.

COSS places those distinct security coordinates on the same causal execution [4]. This document specifies the evidence boundary needed to carry that relationship between systems. It does not define the internal semantics or wire format of PIC, information-flow control (IFC), runtime attestation, or any other coordinate.

section.name: Requirements Notation
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [2] [3] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

section.name: Scope
section.t: This specification defines:

list.t: the logical contents of a COSS Temporal Evidence Record;
the binding of coordinate evidence to one execution occurrence and its causal predecessor set;
the distinction between Proof of Possession (PoP), Proof of Relationship (PoR), and Proof of Continuity (PoC);
ordered verification of ordinary continuations, joins, and explicit authorized relaxations; and
the limits of digest references and external evidence.

section.t: This specification does not define a serialization, signature suite, transport, evidence-retention system, PIC representation, IFC model, or product-specific mapping. Profiles define those choices. A mapping to an execution-evidence system is a profile of this specification, not a redefinition of PIC or COSS semantics.

section.name: One Effect, Several Questions
section.t: Alice authorizes reading her documents for a verification. Bob independently authorizes sending official email. Carol is an AI agent; in the accepted variant below, Carol acts as a Data Loss Prevention (DLP) service. Trent stores Alice's documents. Dave is a mail service whose rule forbids confidential data over email.

figure.artwork:
Alice -- read her documents, for verification --\ \ Bob -- send official email --------------------> Carol -- send(bytes) --> Dave / Trent -- Alice's documents; classification HIGH /
Dave's rule: no confidential data by email

section.t: The two permissions can be individually valid while the proposed effect remains inadmissible. Dave receives a permission and bytes:

figure.artwork:
send request permission: send email bytes: 52 65 6c 61 7a 69 6f 6e 65 ...
authority question: may this occurrence send email? flow question: may these bytes flow to this destination? causal question: which earlier occurrences produced this request and these bytes?

section.t: Neither the bytes nor the send permission answers all three questions. A log entry with an actor and timestamp does not establish the causal relationship. Evidence is sufficient for this effect only when the relevant answers are bound to the same occurrence.

section.name: One Causal Axis
section.t: Let e be an execution occurrence and Pred(e) its represented immediate causal predecessors. Its represented history is the causal down-set Hist(e), not a wall-clock interval and not a second timeline per security mechanism [4] [7].

figure.artwork: Alice intent ----> Trent release -----\ > Carol send request ----> Dave effect Bob intent --------------------------/

section.t: Common ancestry, equal timestamps, the same executor, or co-residence in one process MUST NOT be treated as proof that two branches are the same continuation. A claimed predecessor edge requires profile-defined, causally sound evidence.

section.name: COSS Security State
section.t: For a finite set of coordinate profiles J, the security state at occurrence e is:

figure.artwork: Sigma(e) = (sigma_j(e)) for every j in J

section.t: Each profile j defines:

list.t: its state space;
its order <=_j, meaning "no more permissive than";
the behaviors admitted by a state; and
the evidence and verification procedure that establish its claims.

section.t: For an ordinary causal edge p -> e, COSS continuity requires:

figure.artwork: PoR(p, e) AND sigma_j(e) <=_j sigma_j(p) for every required j

section.t: PIC is the authority coordinate of this construction. For set-valued PIC authority C, the order is set inclusion:

figure.artwork: PoR(p, e) AND C(e) subset-of C(p)

section.t: An IFC profile may provide a different state and order. COSS does not require distinct coordinates to use the same vocabulary, verifier, or artifact format. It requires their results to constrain the same occurrence.
At an ordinary multi-parent join, the child MUST be no more permissive than every parent in every required coordinate. For PIC authority:

figure.artwork: C(e) subset-of intersection of C(p), for every p in Pred(e)

section.t: A grant, authority composition, declassification, endorsement, or other non-conservative change MUST be represented as an explicit authorized relaxation. It MUST NOT be presented as an ordinary continuation.

section.name: PoP, PoR, and PoC in COSS Evidence
section.t: PoP, PoR, and PoC answer different questions:

texttable.c: Does the presenter control a key or artifact?
Authenticates possession. It does not identify the causal occurrence.
Does this occurrence validly continue this specific predecessor?
Establishes a profile-defined causal edge and binds the successor to the predecessor record.
Does the whole represented execution preserve valid continuation?
Composes accepted PoR edges and coordinate refinement across the causal history.

section.t: PoP MAY protect a COSS record or a referenced artifact, but PoP alone MUST NOT be accepted as PoR or PoC. A digest chain establishes artifact linkage only. It establishes COSS continuity only when the applicable profiles also validate the causal relationships and coordinate rules.

PIC PoC is the authority specialization. COSS product continuity applies the same causal composition to every required ordered coordinate. There is one predecessor graph; there is not an unrelated "PIC chain" and "IFC chain" later correlated by time or actor name.

section.name: COSS Temporal Evidence Record
section.t: A COSS Temporal Evidence Record TE(e) is an authenticated commitment with the following logical fields:

texttable.c: The exact COSS evidence specification or profile version.
A commitment to the concrete execution occurrence.
An identifier or commitment for the trusted policy that selects required coordinates and verification rules.
Digest references to the exact authenticated predecessor records.
A commitment to the request, message, or protected effect being judged.
Typed references to occurrence, causal, or coordinate evidence.
For an authorized relaxation, references to its separate authorization and affected coordinates.

section.t: Every digest reference MUST identify the digest algorithm and the digest of the exact referenced bytes. The profile MUST define which bytes are hashed. A locator MAY accompany a digest but MUST NOT be trusted for identity or integrity.
An evidence entry declares one or more roles:

list.t: occurrence evidence describes what ran or which concrete request, message, or effect occurred;
causal evidence supports one or more claimed predecessor relationships; and
coordinate evidence supports a state, refinement, or admission result under a named coordinate profile.

section.t: One artifact MAY fulfill several roles. A runtime or provenance record is not automatically a security-state coordinate: it becomes coordinate evidence only under a profile that defines its state, order, admitted behavior, and verifier.

A coordinate-evidence entry MUST identify its coordinate and exact profile version. It MUST also carry or commit to the coordinate state established for the occurrence and reference the evidence from which that result is verified. The state MAY remain selectively disclosed if the profile supplies a proof sufficient for refinement and admission.

A root record has no predecessors. An ordinary or authorized-relaxation record has one or more distinct predecessors. The resolved predecessor relation MUST be acyclic. A profile MUST NOT infer a missing predecessor from physical time or list order.

section.name: Same-Occurrence Binding
section.t: Every required evidence entry MUST be bound to the record's occurrence. A profile MAY establish this in either of two ways:

list.t: the evidence artifact directly commits to the same occurrence; or
a trusted handoff boundary authenticates one record that commits together to the occurrence, its predecessor records, and the exact evidence-artifact digests.

section.t: Association performed later from timestamps, actor identifiers, workflow labels, or separately valid artifacts is insufficient. The binding MUST prevent an implementation from pairing valid PIC evidence from one execution with valid IFC or runtime evidence from another.

section.name: References Are Not Validation
section.t: An authenticated digest reference proves that the signer committed to exact artifact bytes. It does not prove that:

list.t: the referenced statement is true;
its issuer is trusted for the claimed role;
the artifact establishes PoR;
its coordinate state is correctly ordered; or
the behavior is admitted.

section.t: Each referenced artifact MUST therefore be resolved, integrity-checked, and independently validated by the verifier required by its declared profile. An unavailable required artifact causes verification to fail unless the selected profile defines an equivalent self-contained proof.

section.t: The following JSON is illustrative and is not a wire format or a registry of identifier strings:

The record binds three external artifacts to one mail-send occurrence. It does not ask the runtime-evidence system to compute PIC attenuation, and it does not ask PIC to decide IFC. Dave validates each required profile and then applies the joint admission rule.

section.name: Minimal Integration Contract
section.t: An execution-evidence system can support COSS Temporal Evidence without implementing PIC or IFC internally. Its profile needs to provide:

list.t: an authenticated record for the concrete occurrence and behavior;
digest references that form the represented predecessor graph;
typed digest references to external coordinate evidence;
same-occurrence binding for those references; and
a way for the receiving verifier to invoke, or validate the result of, each required coordinate verifier.

section.t: The authority intersection remains a PIC operation. IFC admission remains an IFC operation. The execution-evidence system records and binds the facts on which those independent decisions rely.

section.name: Verification
section.t: A conformant verifier MUST perform the following checks in order:

list.t: Record validation. Parse the record under the selected profile; reject unsupported versions, malformed fields, duplicate coordinate identifiers not explicitly allowed by profile, and unsafe resource consumption.
Record authenticity. Validate the record's integrity, authenticating mechanism, trust anchor, algorithm policy, and profile-defined freshness or replay rules.

Policy selection. Resolve the policy under local trusted configuration and determine the required coordinates, evidence profiles, and verification rules. The producer MUST NOT be able to select a weaker policy for the effect.
Occurrence and behavior binding. Recompute or otherwise validate the commitments to the concrete request, message, or effect being judged.
Reference integrity. Resolve every required artifact and verify its digest over the profile-defined exact bytes.
Evidence validity. Apply the verifier and trust policy declared by every required evidence profile. A reference signature is not a substitute for this step.

Causal validity. Validate that predecessor references are distinct, the resolved graph is acyclic, the declared predecessor set is complete under the selected profile, and the required PoR evidence is valid. Root, ordinary linear, ordinary join, and authorized-relaxation records MUST NOT be confused.
Coordinate continuity. For an ordinary record, verify that every required coordinate is no more permissive than every applicable predecessor under that coordinate's declared order.

Relaxation authorization. For an authorized relaxation, verify its separate authorization, the coordinates it may change, and the new bound. Unaffected coordinates remain subject to ordinary continuity.
Joint admission. Before a protected effect, verify that every coordinate required by policy admits the committed behavior. Any required rejection rejects the effect.

section.t: An implementation MUST fail closed when a required coordinate, artifact, verifier, causal edge, or binding cannot be established. It MUST NOT silently reduce a multi-coordinate decision to the coordinates it happens to understand.

section.name: Rejected Ordinary Path
section.t: For Carol's proposed mail effect, assume the evidence establishes:

figure.artwork: PIC authority: send-email is present IFC provenance: the bytes depend on Alice's HIGH documents destination policy: external email is LOW causal binding: all results refer to this exact send occurrence

section.t: The authority coordinate admits send-email. The IFC coordinate rejects the HIGH -> LOW flow. Dave therefore rejects the effect. PIC does not claim that Carol is physically unable to copy or transmit bytes through an unmediated path; it establishes that such an effect is not a valid admitted continuation. The claimed protection requires the mail effect to pass through Dave or another complete mediation boundary.

section.name: Accepted DLP Path
section.t: Suppose Carol does not initially hold send-email. Bob invokes Carol by combining the read-for-verification authority received from Alice with Bob's own send-email authority. That union is not an ordinary join. It MUST be represented as an explicit authorized composition whose COSS record has transition class authorized-relaxation.
Carol then evaluates the exact candidate output under the selected DLP or IFC profile. Two cases are distinct:

list.t: If the verified output state already admits flow to the destination, no IFC relaxation is needed.

If the output is derived from HIGH input and is released or sanitized for a LOW destination, the change MUST be an explicit authorized declassification. Its evidence MUST bind the input, exact output bytes, applicable policy, and declassification authorization.

section.t: The evidence graph makes both possible security boundaries visible:

figure.artwork: Alice read ----\ > [authorized composition: read + send] ---> Carol · DLP Bob send -----/ | | verifies exact output Trent data ------------------------------------------------->| v [declassification, if required] | v Dave mail effect

section.t: The record presented to Dave binds at least:

figure.artwork: behavior: digest of destination, message, and exact output bytes predecessor: digest of the authenticated predecessor record PIC coordinate evidence: digest of the authorized composition and authority state IFC coordinate evidence: digest of the DLP/IFC result for the exact output relaxation evidence: digest of declassification authorization, when required occurrence evidence: digest of the execution evidence for this handoff

section.t: Dave accepts only if the composition is authorized, the PIC state admits send-email, the DLP or IFC result admits the exact output and destination, any required declassification is authorized, and every item is bound to the same occurrence. Without the required composition or declassification evidence, valid evidence in another coordinate does not repair the missing rule.

section.name: Conformance
section.t: A COSS Temporal Evidence Producer conforms to this specification when it creates authenticated records that bind the occurrence, policy, predecessors, behavior, evidence references, and transition class as required above.

A COSS Temporal Evidence Verifier conforms when it implements the ordered verification procedure, validates every required external profile independently, and fails closed on missing or unsupported required evidence.

A COSS Evidence Profile conforms when it defines the concrete serialization, authenticating mechanism, exact-byte digest rules, occurrence and behavior commitments, coordinate identifiers, coordinate orders, evidence verifiers, freshness rules, and required-coordinate policy needed to realize this specification.
Conformance to this document does not imply conformance to PIC, an IFC system, or any referenced evidence system. Those claims require independent conformance to the corresponding specifications.

section.name: Origins, Authorship, and Historical Record
section.t: This section is informative.

The Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) Model was originally developed by Nicola Gallo as a formal framework for reasoning about causal authority propagation across distributed execution. Its development introduced Proof of Relationship (PoR), Proof of Continuity (PoC), authority non-expansion, relational attenuation, and event-level causal provenance as connected parts of the framework. COSS generalizes the carried security state from authority to a finite product of ordered security coordinates on the same causal occurrence. The PIC Specifications translate those formal results into technical requirements and are published and maintained by Nitro Agility S.r.l. as Specification Steward.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The primary threat addressed by this document is evidence mix-and-match: combining valid evidence from different occurrences so that it appears to justify one effect. Same-occurrence binding and exact predecessor references are REQUIRED to prevent that substitution.

A digest authenticates bytes only through a separately trusted signature or channel and says nothing by itself about semantic truth. Weak, deprecated, ambiguous, or incorrectly canonicalized digest inputs can defeat the binding. Profiles MUST define exact-byte hashing and algorithm-agility policy.

Omitting a coordinate can change a security verdict. Required coordinates MUST therefore be selected by trusted policy, not by the producer. Unknown required coordinates and unavailable required evidence MUST fail closed.

Causal evidence can be incomplete or false. Claims that depend on complete causal ancestry additionally require sound causal evidence, representation of every in-scope cause, and mediation of every protected effect. This specification cannot protect causes or effects omitted from the modeled and mediated execution.
Replay, fan-out, freshness, revocation, trust-anchor compromise, and equivocation remain profile and deployment concerns. A valid historical record is not automatically valid for a new occurrence.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Cross-coordinate evidence can expose principals, software identities, data classifications, locations, causal relationships, and stable execution identifiers. Profiles SHOULD use commitments, selective disclosure, scoped identifiers, and minimum necessary retention while preserving the evidence needed for the claimed security property. Digest references can still enable correlation when the same artifact is reused across domains.

section.name: Registry Considerations
section.t: This version defines no shared protocol registry and requests no external registry action. A future interoperability profile may define registries for coordinate identifiers, evidence roles, media types, digest algorithms, transition classes, or error values.
